examples.en: The presenter slipped on a banana skin during the interview.

meaning.en: It is often used when a person, team, company or government appears successful or confident but is embarrassed by one simple mistake or an unexpectedly difficult situation. Collins defines it as saying or doing something that makes you look stupid and causes problems, while Merriam-Webster describes it as failing in an embarrassing way.
meaning.zh: slip on a banana skin 指某人犯下一個愚蠢或本可避免的錯誤，或意外失敗，結果令自己出醜並引起麻煩。
naturalZh: 在看似容易的事情上失敗
因一時大意而惹上麻煩

register.summaryEn: The expression is mainly British, informal and especially common in journalism, sport and public commentary. Oxford describes banana skin as British and informal, while Collins notes that the figurative use is mainly British and journalistic.

benefits.titleEn: It Expresses More Than “Make a Mistake”
benefits.titleZh: 意思比 make a mistake 更豐富
benefits.en: The idiomatic version suggests that the mistake was foolish, embarrassing and damaging.
benefits.zh: 慣用語版本不只表示「犯錯」，還暗示這個錯誤愚蠢、令人尷尬，而且帶來麻煩。

benefits.en: The expression is especially effective when a successful person or strong team fails over something simple.
benefits.zh: 當成功人士或強隊在簡單事情上失手時，這個表達尤其有力。

benefits.titleZh: 提醒人們不要過分自信
benefits.zh: 不要只因比賽看似容易便放鬆。 我們仍可能意外失手。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful for Public Commentary
benefits.en: political mistakes; sporting defeats; failed product launches; embarrassing interviews; careless public statements.
benefits.zh: 記者和評論員可以用它評論政治失誤、體育爆冷、產品推出失敗、尷尬訪問及大意的公開言論。

benefits.titleEn: It Adds Mild Humour or Irony
benefits.en: The image of a confident person suddenly falling creates a mildly comic tone. However, it should not be used when the real event involves serious suffering.
benefits.zh: 一個充滿自信的人突然滑倒的畫面帶有輕微喜劇效果。 不過，如果真實事件涉及嚴重傷害或苦難，便不應使用。

origin.statusEn: Gradual Development; Exact First Figurative Use Uncertain
origin.statusZh: 逐漸形成；確切首次比喻用法不明

history.en: By 1910, slipping on a banana skin was already being used as an obvious example of physical comedy. A Smithsonian history of banana humour also records the gag in Harold Lloyd’s 1917 silent film The Flirt, while the Library of Congress describes banana peels being used to arrange a comic accident in the 1927 Laurel and Hardy film The Battle of the Century.
history.zh: 早在1910年，踏中香蕉皮滑倒已被視為一種明顯的肢體喜劇例子。 這個橋段其後亦常見於默片及喜劇電影。

history.en: A small and easily avoided object can suddenly bring down somebody who appears confident. The image therefore became a natural metaphor for an unexpected, foolish mistake that causes embarrassment or damages a person’s success. The precise first figurative use has not been firmly identified.
history.zh: 一件細小而且本可避開的物件，可以突然令一個看似充滿信心的人跌倒。 因此，這個畫面逐漸成為比喻，用來形容意外而愚蠢的錯誤，令人出醜或破壞原有成果。

origin.memoryEn: A tiny banana skin can bring down a confident walker; one tiny mistake can bring down a confident person or team.
origin.memoryZh: 一塊小小的香蕉皮可以令自信的行人跌倒；一個小小的錯誤也可以令自信的人或團隊失手。

rules.en: Daniel stepped on a real banana skin and fell.
rules.zh: 踏中真正的香蕉皮而跌倒。 Daniel 在訪問中說錯公司名稱，因低級錯誤而出醜。

questions.answerZh: 無論大熱門是否實力較強，也必須認真作賽，以免在第一圈意外失手。
questions.targetMeaning: It is often used when a person, team, company or government appears successful or confident but is embarrassed by one simple mistake or an unexpectedly difficult situation. Collins defines it as saying or doing something that makes you look stupid and causes problems, while Merriam-Webster describes it as failing in an embarrassing way.

questions.prompt: The department publicly promised a new service before confirming that it had enough workers or equipment. A report says this may already have created an embarrassing problem.
questions.promptZh: 該部門在確認有足夠員工及設備前，已公開承諾提供新服務。一份報告表示，這可能已經造成了一個令人尷尬的問題。
questions.answer: According to the report, the department may already have slipped on a banana skin by promising a service it cannot yet provide.
questions.answerZh: 報告指出，該部門承諾提供一項尚未有能力提供的服務，可能已經犯下尷尬錯誤。

questions.prompt: The council’s project is almost complete, but the final public document still contains incorrect cost figures.
questions.promptZh: 市議會的項目幾乎完成，但最後的公開文件仍載有錯誤的成本數字。
questions.answer: Unless the incorrect figures are corrected before publication, the council could slip on a banana skin at the very end of the project.
questions.answerZh: 除非錯誤數字在公布前得到修正，否則市議會可能會在項目最後階段因低級錯誤而失手。
